topic: How to Read a Commercial Rent Roll
caption:
A rent roll is one of the most practical tools for underwriting a commercial property, monitoring income, and spotting tenant risk. Start by confirming tenant names, lease dates, and rent frequency. Reconcile the rent roll to bank deposits and lease files, and flag any short payments, free rent, or unidentified concessions. Pay attention to clusters of expirations and tenant concentration—these are risk areas for any owner in Chester County or Montgomery County. Use the rent roll with expense allocations to estimate net cash flow and to prioritize due diligence items during a sale or refinance. Need help reviewing a rent roll or preparing one for listing? Visit dmsellscre.com/investors for guidance and templates tailored to local commercial properties.
